title: Leath Cuinn and Leath Moga
extract: The Leath Cuinn (Conn's Half) and Leath Moga (Mogha's Half) are the two legendary fifth-century divisions of Ireland. According to the Lebor Gabála Érenn (Book of Invasions), the High King of Ireland Conn Cétchathach (Conn of the Hundred Battles) divided Ireland between his son Art mac Cuinn and Mogha Nuadat, a rival of the Érainn. Conn took Leath Cuinn (the northern half) for Art, and Mogha took Leath Moga (the southern half). The boundaries of the two halves were traditionally drawn along the Esker Riada (Irish: Eiscir Riada), a system of eskers that runs roughly from Dublin Bay on the east coast to Galway Bay on the west coast. The northern half (Leath Cuinn) comprised Connacht, Ulster, and Meath; the southern half (Leath Moga) comprised Munster and Leinster. Conn Cétchathach is the legendary common ancestor of both the Connachta dynasty (the royal kindreds of Connacht, including the Uí Briúin and Uí Fiachrach) AND the Uí Néill dynasty (the royal kindreds of Ulster and Meath, including the Northern Uí Néill and Southern Uí Néill).
